hypotheses.paper: O un voisinage ouvert de S, φ une carte compatible de O

hypotheses.note: M, N ∈ φ.source (presupposed by the formula); M, N ∈ S then follows
Déf. 7's notation (m, m') is the CLOSED segment (scan p. 238 checked); φ(M), φ(N) not diametrically opposite (Déf. 7's standing hypothesis); affine case Mathlib's segment

questions: « segments d'extrémités » (l.411) read « segment » (singular), a misprint already noted in the transcription.
(φ(M), φ(N)) is read as Déf. 7's closed segment (round brackets; Déf. 7 writes the open one )m, m'( ), not the open segment; consequently M, N ∈ S. Confirm.
The chart is required to be defined at M and N (needed for φ(M), φ(N) to make sense); with M, N ∈ φ.source this is equivalent to M, N ∈ S.

labels.label: bzdef:c1s1d15_homogene_balayable_divisible

hypotheses.paper: le groupe G des automorphismes projectifs de V
hypotheses.note: GXAut G X V: homeomorphisms that are morphisms both ways (the isomorphisms of the category of p. 238); every bijective morphism is one (GXAut.ofBijective)
for V locally compact, automatic for manifolds on S(n) or ℝⁿ (_proj, _aff corollaries); properness and freeness are not used

questions: Prose l.432–433 « Si V est une variété localement projective et compacte, son revêtement universel est divisible » is NOT formalized here: by DEC-122 it is now its own ledger row bzthm:c1s1_revetement_universel_divisible (transcription l.431–434, an enonce wrapper), bucket D, out of scope for this package (no universal covering / deck group at this pin).

« proprement discontinu » taken in Mathlib's sense per DEC-120 and « sans point fixe » as a free action (IsCancelSMul), consistent with Structure/Quotient. The prose « Il est clair que toute variété divisible (ou homogène) est balayable » is l.436.

labels.label: bzdef:c1s1d16_maximale

hypotheses.note: ConnectedSpace V is part of IsMaximal

hypotheses.paper: U variété connexe localement projective de même dimension
hypotheses.note: same model X, ConnectedSpace U, « variété » read Hausdorff (T2Space U) — ruled by DEC-122 (« Déf. 16's compact ⇒ maximal is read with U Hausdorff »). Second countability of U is not imposed and U ranges over V's universe: dropping second countability ENLARGES the class of U (IsMaximal a priori stronger than the F6 reading), the universe restriction makes it a priori weaker; for second countable V the two definitions agree (SCOPE: U' = f(V) ∪ a connected chart ball at a point of closure f(V) ∖ f(V) is open, connected, Hausdorff, second countable, f : V → U' is not onto, and |U'| ≤ |V| + 𝔠 so U' is small in V's universe).

hypotheses.paper: V isomorphe à un ouvert de U, distinct de U
hypotheses.note: IsMaximal uses an injective morphism V → U; the literal form (an open W ≠ U with an isomorphism V ≃ W for the open-subset structure) is proved equivalent: isMaximal_iff / exists_opens_iso_iff

hypotheses.paper: prose l.478: une variété compacte est maximale
hypotheses.note: isMaximal_of_compactSpace: V compact connected; uses U Hausdorff (the ruled reading)

questions: RULED (DEC-122): « variété » U is read Hausdorff; without it « une variété compacte est évidemment maximale » fails (S(1) is a proper open subset of the circle with one point doubled; described, not formalized).

Corrected (AUDIT-1 minor): the earlier sentence « second countability of U is not needed and only shrinks the class of U » pointed the wrong way. Dropping it enlarges the class of U; the definitions nevertheless agree for second countable V by the U' = f(V) ∪ (chart ball) argument stated in SCOPE (not formalized; isMaximal_iff_secondCountable not proved).
